title: Time-Resolved Atomic-Resolution 3D Brownian Tomography of Nanocrystals in Liquid
content: Colloidal nanocrystals are an important class of materials whose properties can be finely tuned by slight changes in their atomic structure. Furthermore, colloidal nanocrystals often exhibit structural transformations that are not found in their bulk counterparts. For example, nanocrystals as small as a few nanometers melt at lower temperatures than their bulk counterparts [1], and nanocrystals may exhibit phases that are thermodynamically metastable in the bulk phase diagram [2]. These structural transformations are generally attributed to the dominant role of surface in smaller nanocrystals [3]. However, detailed understanding of these transformations has been limited by the lack of an experimental method capable of obtaining time-resolved, three-dimensional (3D) atomic structures of nanocrystals in solution.
